Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15 14:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marta Lopez (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (CTO, Meridian), Leah Kim (Lead ML Engineer), Omar Ruiz (Platform Eng)

Auto-summary (auto gen may be noisy): customer wants to understand how Redwood would fit into their hybrid infra, specifically where gateway/proxy sits vs sidecar, how SDKs integrate with LangChain and LamaIndex, question on private VPC deployment and KMS, also tokens and quotas.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um — quick roll call. we're on a 50 minute slot, we'll go through architecture, integration points, then close with next steps.
[00:12] Ravi (Meridian): yep thanks, i'm ravi — CTO. quick context: we run a mix of cloud (GCP us-west) and colo in ashburn; latency sensitive features run from colo. we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for inference.
[00:25] Leah (Meridian): hi all, leah here. we use LangChain a lot for retrieval-augmented generation workflows, and LlamaIndex in a few pipelines — maybe you heard it as LamaIndex sometimes.
[00:38] Marta (Redwood): totally — we see that pattern a lot. quick question: do you have a preference for SDK integration (server-side calls) vs routing through a central gateway?
[00:46] Omar (Meridian): our infra team prefers a gateway/proxy pattern so we can enforce auth, rate limits, and inspect traffic. sidecar options are ok if they don't add too much overhead.
[00:59] Avery (Redwood): that's helpful. rough map: hosted API is fastest to get started but we send requests out of your VPC via our egress rules; dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput; private offers a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem.
[01:17] Ravi (Meridian): for data residency and compliance we lean private, but we need to validate cost. also KMS integration and audit logs are must-haves, SOC2 as baseline.
[01:28] Marta (Redwood): we support KMS/HSM integrations and per-tenant audit logs in our private offering; for dedicated we can provide a customer-only cluster with encrypted disks and audit forwarding.
[01:38] Leah (Meridian): practical question on LangChain: do you have first-class SDK adapters or do we rewrite connectors?
[01:46] Marta (Redwood): we have examples and adapter snippets. typically customers wrap our SDK in a connector class, or we provide a small shim that fits into LangChain's LLMChain/LLM wrapper. i'll share a sample repo link after.
[01:58] Omar (Meridian): and for LlamaIndex — we actually use a custom docstore; any caveats with kv-cache and streaming?
[02:07] Marta (Redwood): we handle KV cache at the runtime layer — streaming and kv cache interplay is supported but you should watch sequence lengths and prefix cache hit rates; some customers see cost wins by enabling prefix caching for chat-style workloads.
[02:24] Avery (Redwood): also note, when folks use LlamaIndex, tokenization differences matter — small variance in token counts across model variants. that'll affect cost projections.
[02:36] Ravi (Meridian): can you talk about rate limits and quotas — we want per-team quotas and burst policies, not just account-level throttle.
[02:46] Marta (Redwood): yes, Redwood Console supports token-level quotas per API key and per-route rate limiting. you can set steady-state QPS and burst allowances. we also expose hooks for a gateway to surface rate-limit headers so you can enforce at the edge.
[02:59] Omar (Meridian): great, we want the gateway to be able to know token budgets before forwarding to Redwood. is there a lightweight preflight call?
[03:07] Avery (Redwood): we have a tokens-estimate endpoint and a dry-run mode to calculate token usage without eating quota; for higher performance some customers run an edge estimator in the gateway using local tokenization libs.
[03:20] Leah (Meridian): observability — we need request-level tracing, span IDs that join with our Jaeger traces, and per-route latency metrics exported to Prometheus. is that supported?
[03:32] Marta (Redwood): yes, we emit OpenTelemetry-compatible traces and metrics. in hosted mode we provide tracing headers and an ingest pipeline; in private you can deploy collectors inside the VPC so traces never leave the network.
[03:43] Ravi (Meridian): curious about canary rollouts and fallback — if a heavy model saturates, can requests fall back to a smaller model automatically?
[03:52] Avery (Redwood): absolutely — rollout policies let you route e.g., 5% to new model and fallback rules to a cheaper variant on high latency or errors. that lives in the routing layer and is configurable per-route.
[04:05] Omar (Meridian): about gateway pattern — do you recommend sidecar per service or a central proxy? pros/cons?
[04:13] Marta (Redwood): sidecars give you per-node caching and lower network hops but add complexity; central proxy simplifies ops and policy but can be a bottleneck. many customers start central and then move critical services to sidecar for latency-sensitive endpoints.
[04:29] Leah (Meridian): onboarding effort — what's the minimal pilot to validate latency and cost?
[04:35] Avery (Redwood): we suggest: 1) provide sample prompt set and traffic profile; 2) Redwood runs hosted spikes and a dedicated run with similar QPS; 3) compare 99th pctl latency and cost per 1M tokens. typical pilot runs 2–4 weeks.
[04:50] Ravi (Meridian): do you have sample benchmark suites? we'd rather not build infra to test every model variant.
[04:57] Marta (Redwood): yes — we'll share a benchmark spreadsheet and a runner script that can replay prompts at target concurrency. it supports model variants and quantization profiles.
[05:08] Leah (Meridian): security — SSO, RBAC, SCIM for provisioning teams. we need to map roles to product features.
[05:16] Avery (Redwood): we integrate SAML/SSO, have RBAC roles and SCIM provisioning. in private deployments you can sync with your existing IdP.
[05:25] Omar (Meridian): what about cost controls — is there a kill-switch for runaway prompts?
[05:31] Marta (Redwood): you can configure per-key hard quotas and soft alerts with webhooks. the gateway can also enforce a token cap per request.
[05:42] Ravi (Meridian): any notable gotchas for on-prem? network latency to your control plane?
[05:49] Avery (Redwood): for private deployments the control plane can be customer-managed; if you choose hosted control plane with private data plane, there are heartbeats and occasional control traffic — we document that. latency is primarily between your app and the runtime; place the runtime near your colo to minimize hops.
[06:05] Leah (Meridian): do you support containerized on-prem package, helm charts?
[06:10] Marta (Redwood): yes, helm charts and an air-gapped bundle for highly regulated customers.
[06:18] Ravi (Meridian): let's talk numbers — our expected peak is ~600 qps for short-chat flows, average payload ~1.2k tokens, 95th pctl latency target < 350ms. cost target is under $X per 1k requests but we'll share specifics.
[06:33] Avery (Redwood): good, please send that fully specified. with 600 qps we may recommend dedicated or private depending on sustained vs spiky; we can model cost once we have token distributions.
[06:45] Omar (Meridian): how does the SDK handle streaming and reconnects? we need idempotent responses for retry logic.
[06:52] Marta (Redwood): SDK supports chunked streaming and resumable sessions; we expose request IDs and deterministic fallback tokens so retries are traceable.
[07:03] Leah (Meridian): any latency overhead if we go through central proxy?
[07:08] Avery (Redwood): expect small added latency — often 10–30msdepending on colocations. sidecar reduces that but increases deployment surface.
[07:18] Ravi (Meridian): do you have references who did on-prem pilot recently?
[07:22] Avery (Redwood): yes — happy to share a case study (we'll anonymize specifics) where a customer moved from hosted to dedicated to reduce unit costs and moved critical low-latency paths to sidecars.
[07:33] Omar (Meridian): about model variants — do you support running quantized models for cheaper inference? what's the perf hit?
[07:41] Marta (Redwood): we support quantization profiles; some models retain quality with 4-bit quant, others degrade. our Optimize tooling recommends quantization per workload and provides regression alerts on eval sets.
[07:55] Leah (Meridian): we'll need eval harness to ensure quality doesn't regress.
[08:00] Marta (Redwood): included — we can hook your evals into Redwood Optimize and run periodic checks.
[08:08] Ravi (Meridian): okay — final: timeline. we want to start pilot next week if possible and have a decision in 6 weeks. can you meet that?
[08:16] Avery (Redwood): yes, we can prioritize. Marta will prep LangChain/LlamaIndex samples and the security kit.
[08:24] Omar (Meridian): who will be the technical owner on your side for the pilot?
[08:28] Marta (Redwood): that'll be me — i'll be the SE lead.
[08:32] Avery (Redwood): i'll handle commercial and kickoff coordination.
[08:36] Leah (Meridian): okay, let's recap next steps.
[08:40] Ravi (Meridian): recap: redwood sends security docs, sample adapters, benchmark runner; meridian sends prompt set, payload sizes, qps numbers. set kickoff for 2026-09-27.
[08:53] Avery (Redwood): perfect — i'll create calendar invite and shared drive link, and i'll drop the SOC2 doc and benchmark template in there.
[09:00] Marta (Redwood): action items noted. any other questions?
[09:05] Leah (Meridian): none from me. thanks.
[09:08] Ravi (Meridian): thanks everyone.
[09:12] Avery (Redwood): thanks, bye.
